q: भारतीय संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद के अंतर्गत भारत के राष्ट्रपति पर महाभियोग (Impeachment) की प्रक्रिया दी गई है तथा यह किस एकमात्र आधार पर चलाया जा सकता है?
e:
Article 61 prescribes the quasi-judicial impeachment procedure of the President solely on the ground of 'Violation of the Constitution' (संविधान का अतिक्रमण). It can be initiated in either House of Parliament with 14 days' prior notice signed by at least 1/4th of total members and passed by a 2/3rd majority of the TOTAL membership of each House.
अनुच्छेद 61 के अंतर्गत केवल 'संविधान के अतिक्रमण' के आधार पर राष्ट्रपति पर महाभियोग चलाया जा सकता है।
Booster Facts: (1) Both elected AND nominated members of Parliament participate in impeachment, whereas State Assemblies do NOT participate (exact opposite of Presidential election under Art. 54). (2) No Indian President has been impeached so far.
qe: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the procedure for the Impeachment of the President of India laid down, and on what sole ground can it be initiated?

q: भारत के किस राष्ट्रपति ने 1986 में भारतीय डाकघर (संशोधन) विधेयक पर न तो हस्ताक्षर किए और न ही उसे लौटाया, और इस प्रकार 'जेबी वीटो' (Pocket Veto) का प्रसिद्ध प्रयोग किया?
e:
President Giani Zail Singh exercised the Pocket Veto in 1986 on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill (passed by Rajiv Gandhi's government) because Article 111 prescribes no time limit for the President to act on a Bill.
राष्ट्रपति ज्ञानी जैल सिंह ने 1986 में भारतीय डाकघर (संशोधन) विधेयक पर जेबी वीटो का प्रयोग किया था।
Booster Facts: (1) Three Vetoes of Indian President: Absolute Veto (used by Dr. Rajendra Prasad on PEPSU Appropriation Bill, 1954), Suspensive Veto (overridden by simple majority), and Pocket Veto. (2) Indian President has NO veto power over Constitutional Amendment Bills (made mandatory by 24th Amendment Act, 1971).
qe: Which President of India famously exercised the 'Pocket Veto' (जेबी वीटो) in 1986 by neither signing nor returning the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill?

q: अनुच्छेद 123 के अंतर्गत भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा प्रख्यापित अध्यादेश (Ordinance) को संसद के पुनः समवेत होने के कितने समय के भीतर दोनों सदनों से अनुमोदित होना आवश्यक है, अन्यथा वह समाप्त हो जाता है?
e:
Under Article 123, a Presidential Ordinance ceases to operate at the expiration of 6 weeks from the reassembly of Parliament unless approved by both Houses. Since the maximum gap between two sessions is 6 months (Art. 85), the maximum possible life of an unapproved ordinance is 6 months and 6 weeks.
संसद की पुनः बैठक के 6 सप्ताह के भीतर अनुमोदन अनिवार्य है (अधिकतम अवधि: 6 माह + 6 सप्ताह)।
Booster Facts: (1) Ordinance-making is a legislative power of the President exercised only when at least one House is not in session. (2) In D.C. Wadhwa (1987) and Krishna Kumar Singh (2017), the Supreme Court held that repeated repromulgation of ordinances is a fraud on the Constitution.
qe: Under Article 123, an Ordinance promulgated by the President of India must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within what period from the reassembly of Parliament, failing which it ceases to operate?

q:
44वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1978 के पश्चात् अनुच्छेद 352 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल के संबंध में निम्नलिखित दो कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: 'आंतरिक अशांति' (Internal Disturbance) के आधार को बदलकर 'सशस्त्र विद्रोह' (Armed Rebellion) कर दिया गया।
कथन II: राष्ट्रपति केवल केंद्रीय मंत्रिमंडल (Cabinet) की लिखित सिफारिश प्राप्त होने के बाद ही राष्ट्रीय आपातकाल की उद्घोषणा कर सकते हैं।
उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं?
o: Neither Statement I nor Statement II
Both Statement I and Statement II
e:
Both statements are correct reforms introduced by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 (which also inserted the word 'Cabinet' for the only time in the Constitution under Article 352).
कथन I और कथन II दोनों 44वें संशोधन (1978) द्वारा किए गए प्रमुख प्रावधान हैं।
Booster Facts: (1) Three Emergency provisions: Art. 352 (National Emergency — proclaimed 3 times: 1962, 1971, 1975), Art. 356 (President's Rule), Art. 360 (Financial Emergency — never proclaimed). (2) Articles 20 and 21 can NEVER be suspended even during a National Emergency (44th Amendment).
qe:
Consider the following two statements regarding National Emergency under Article 352 after the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978:
Statement I: The ground 'Internal Disturbance' was replaced by 'Armed Rebellion'.
Statement II: The President can proclaim a National Emergency only after receiving a written recommendation from the Union Cabinet.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
oe: Neither Statement I nor Statement II
Both Statement I and Statement II

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 72 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रपति की कौन-सी क्षमादान शक्ति दण्ड के एक स्वरूप को बदलकर अपेक्षाकृत हल्के स्वरूप में परिवर्तित करती है (जैसे मृत्युदण्ड को कठोर कारावास में बदलना)?
e:
Commutation (लघुकरण) substitutes one form of punishment with a lighter form (e.g., Death → Life imprisonment). Remission reduces duration without changing nature; Respite awards lesser sentence due to special facts (e.g., pregnancy/disability); Reprieve grants temporary stay of execution.
दण्ड की प्रकृति बदलकर हल्का करना 'लघुकरण (Commutation)' कहलाता है।
Booster Facts: (1) President (Art. 72) can pardon death sentences and court-martial punishments, whereas Governor (Art. 161) CANNOT pardon a death sentence or court-martial sentence.
qe: Under Article 72 of the Indian Constitution, which pardoning power of the President substitutes one form of punishment for a lighter form (e.g., changing a death sentence to rigorous imprisonment)?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 75(3) के अनुसार, केंद्रीय मंत्रिपरिषद सामूहिक रूप से किसके प्रति उत्तरदायी होती है?
o: The Lok Sabha (House of the People)
e:
Article 75(3) states that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible specifically to the Lok Sabha ("swim and sink together"). Individually, ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President under Article 75(2).
अनुच्छेद 75(3) के अनुसार केंद्रीय मंत्रिपरिषद सामूहिक रूप से केवल 'लोकसभा' के प्रति उत्तरदायी होती है।
Booster Facts: (1) A No-Confidence Motion can be moved ONLY in the Lok Sabha (requires support of at least 50 MPs). (2) Similarly, State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Vidhan Sabha under Article 164(2).
qe: According to Article 75(3) of the Indian Constitution, the Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
oe: The Lok Sabha (House of the People)

q: किस संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम ने केंद्रीय मंत्रिपरिषद में प्रधानमंत्री सहित मंत्रियों की कुल संख्या को लोकसभा की कुल सदस्य संख्या के 15% तक सीमित कर दिया?
e:
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 added Article 75(1A) (and Art. 164(1A) for States) capping the size of the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha (or State Legislative Assembly, with a minimum of 12 ministers in smaller states; 10% for Delhi).
91वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2003 द्वारा मंत्रिपरिषद का आकार 15% तक सीमित किया गया।
Booster Facts: (1) The 91st Amendment also strengthened the Anti-Defection Law by omitting the 1/3rd 'split' exception in the Tenth Schedule.
qe: Which Constitutional Amendment Act capped the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Union Council of Ministers at 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha?

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद राष्ट्रपति को मंत्रिपरिषद के निर्णयों और प्रशासन संबंधी जानकारी देने के प्रधानमंत्री के कर्तव्यों का स्पष्ट उल्लेख करता है?
e:
Article 78 defines the constitutional duties of the Prime Minister as the principal channel of communication between the Council of Ministers and the President.
अनुच्छेद 78 राष्ट्रपति को जानकारी देने के प्रधानमंत्री के कर्तव्यों से संबंधित है।
Booster Facts: (1) Article 74 = Council of Ministers to aid and advise President. (2) Article 75 = Appointment & provisions as to Ministers. (3) Article 76 = Attorney General of India. (4) Counterpart for Chief Minister & Governor is Article 167.
qe: Which Article of the Indian Constitution explicitly enumerates the duties of the Prime Minister with respect to furnishing information and decisions of the Council of Ministers to the President?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 79 के अंतर्गत भारत की संसद किससे मिलकर बनती है?
o: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha only
The President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha
President, Vice-President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha
e:
Article 79 declares that Parliament consists of the President and the two Houses — the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha). The President is an integral part of Parliament because no bill becomes law without Presidential assent.
अनुच्छेद 79 के अनुसार संसद = राष्ट्रपति + राज्यसभा + लोकसभा।
Booster Facts: (1) Art. 80 = Rajya Sabha (max 250; 238 elected + 12 nominated). (2) Art. 81 = Lok Sabha (Anglo-Indian nomination removed by 104th Amendment Act, 2019).
qe: Under Article 79 of the Indian Constitution, the Parliament of India consists of:
oe: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha only
The President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha
President, Vice-President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha

q: भारतीय संसद में 'धन विधेयक' (अनुच्छेद 110) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: It can be introduced ONLY in the Lok Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President.
The decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final.
The Rajya Sabha can retain a Money Bill for a maximum period of 14 days.
A Joint Sitting of both Houses under Article 108 can be summoned to resolve a deadlock over a Money Bill.
e:
Statement D is NOT correct: there is NO provision for a Joint Sitting (Art. 108) for a Money Bill or a Constitutional Amendment Bill, because the Lok Sabha has overriding authority on Money Bills.
विकल्प D असत्य है क्योंकि धन विधेयक पर संयुक्त बैठक (अनुच्छेद 108) का कोई प्रावधान नहीं है।
Booster Facts: (1) Article 109 lays down the special procedure for Money Bills; Article 110 defines Money Bill. (2) Financial Bills (I & II) are governed by Article 117(1) and 117(3).
qe: Which of the following statements regarding a 'Money Bill' (Article 110) in the Indian Parliament is NOT correct?
oe: It can be introduced ONLY in the Lok Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President.
The decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final.
The Rajya Sabha can retain a Money Bill for a maximum period of 14 days.
A Joint Sitting of both Houses under Article 108 can be summoned to resolve a deadlock over a Money Bill.

q: 1950 से अब तक विधायी गतिरोध को दूर करने के लिए अनुच्छेद 108 के अंतर्गत संसद के दोनों सदनों की संयुक्त बैठक कितनी बार बुलाई गई है?
e:
A Joint Sitting under Article 108 has been convened exactly THREE times: (1) Dowry Prohibition Bill, 1961; (2) Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill, 1978; and (3) Prevention of Terrorism Bill (POTA), 2002.
अनुच्छेद 108 के तहत संयुक्त बैठक अब तक केवल तीन बार (1961, 1978, 2002) बुलाई गई है।
Booster Facts: (1) Joint Sitting is summoned by the President (Art. 108) and presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker (Art. 118(4)) — in Speaker's absence, Deputy Speaker, then Deputy Chairman of RS (NEVER the Chairman/Vice-President).
qe: Since 1950, how many times has a Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament under Article 108 been convened to resolve a legislative deadlock?

q: किन दो अनुच्छेदों के अंतर्गत राज्यसभा को ऐसी अनन्य विशेष शक्तियाँ प्राप्त हैं जो लोकसभा को प्राप्त नहीं हैं?
e:
Rajya Sabha has two exclusive powers (by 2/3rd present & voting majority): (1) Article 249 — authorizing Parliament to legislate on a State List subject in national interest; (2) Article 312 — authorizing Parliament to create new All India Services.
अनुच्छेद 249 (राज्य सूची पर कानून) तथा अनुच्छेद 312 (नई अखिल भारतीय सेवा) राज्यसभा की अनन्य शक्तियाँ हैं।
Booster Facts: (1) A resolution for the removal of the Vice-President can also be initiated ONLY in the Rajya Sabha (Article 67(b)).
qe: Under which two Articles does the Rajya Sabha enjoy exclusive special powers NOT shared by the Lok Sabha?

q:
सूची-I (संसदीय वित्तीय समिति) को सूची-II (सदस्य संख्या एवं संरचना) से सुमेलित कीजिए:
सूची-I:
1. लोक लेखा समिति (PAC)
2. प्राक्कलन समिति (Estimates Committee)
3. सार्वजनिक उपक्रम समिति (COPU)
सूची-II:
(a) 30 सदस्य — सभी केवल लोकसभा से
(b) 22 सदस्य (15 लो.स. + 7 रा.स.) — CAG की ऑडिट रिपोर्ट की जाँच
(c) 22 सदस्य (15 लो.स. + 7 रा.स.) — 1964 में कृष्ण मेनन समिति की सिफारिश पर गठित
e:
PAC = 22 (15 LS + 7 RS), chaired by an Opposition leader by convention since 1967, examines CAG reports; Estimates Committee = 30 members all from LS (largest committee, 'continuous economy committee'); COPU = 22 (15 LS + 7 RS, 1964).
सही सुमेलन 1-(b), 2-(a), 3-(c) है।
Booster Facts: (1) Ministers CANNOT be members of any of these three financial committees. (2) PAC and Estimates Committee are called 'Twin Sisters'.
qe:
Match List-I (Parliamentary Financial Committee) with List-II (Strength & Composition):
List-I:
1. Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
2. Estimates Committee
3. Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU)
List-II:
(a) 30 members — ALL from Lok Sabha only
(b) 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS) — examines CAG audit reports
(c) 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS) — created in 1964 on Krishna Menon Committee report

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 100(3) के अंतर्गत संसद के किसी भी सदन की बैठक के लिए न्यूनतम गणपूर्ति (Quorum) कितनी होती है?
e:
Article 100(3) fixes the Quorum at one-tenth (1/10) of the total membership of the House, including the Presiding Officer (i.e., 55 in Lok Sabha and 25 in Rajya Sabha).
गणपूर्ति कुल सदस्य संख्या का दसवाँ भाग (1/10) होती है।
Booster Facts: (1) 'Zero Hour' (12 noon, immediately after Question Hour) is an Indian parliamentary innovation (since 1962) not mentioned in the Rules of Procedure. (2) Adjournment is done by the Presiding Officer; Prorogation and Dissolution by the President.
qe: Under Article 100(3) of the Indian Constitution, what is the minimum Quorum required to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament?

q: भारत सरकार तथा एक या अधिक राज्यों के बीच के विवाद भारत के सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की किस अधिकारिता (अनुच्छेद 131) के अंतर्गत आते हैं?
e:
Article 131 confers exclusive Original Jurisdiction (आरंभिक अधिकारिता) on the Supreme Court to adjudicate federal disputes between Centre and States or between States.
केंद्र-राज्य या अंतर्राज्यीय विवाद अनुच्छेद 131 के तहत सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की 'आरंभिक अधिकारिता' में आते हैं।
Booster Facts: (1) Inter-state water disputes (Art. 262) and pre-constitutional treaties are excluded from Art. 131. (2) Appellate Jurisdiction = Arts. 132–134; Special Leave = Art. 136; Review = Art. 137.
qe: Disputes between the Government of India and one or more States fall under which jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India (Article 131)?

q: भारतीय संविधान में 'न्यायिक पुनर्विलोकन' (Judicial Review) की शक्ति — जो न्यायालयों को संविधान के विरुद्ध कानूनों को रद्द करने का अधिकार देती है — किस देश से ली गई है और मुख्यतः किस अनुच्छेद पर आधारित है?
e:
Judicial Review is borrowed from the US Constitution (Marbury v. Madison, 1803) and is rooted in Article 13 (laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void) read with Articles 32 and 226. It is part of the Basic Structure (Minerva Mills, 1980).
न्यायिक पुनर्विलोकन की अवधारणा अमेरिका से ली गई है तथा अनुच्छेद 13 (व 32, 226) में निहित है।
Booster Facts: (1) The exact phrase 'Judicial Review' is NOT explicitly written in the Constitution, though its substance is built into Arts. 13, 32, 131–136, 226.
qe: The power of 'Judicial Review' (न्यायिक पुनर्विलोकन) in the Indian Constitution — enabling courts to strike down laws violating Fundamental Rights or the Constitution — is borrowed from which country and anchored primarily in which Article?

q: किस ऐतिहासिक सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के निर्णय में सर्वोच्च व उच्च न्यायालय के न्यायाधीशों की नियुक्ति हेतु 'कॉलेजियम प्रणाली' (Collegium System) की औपचारिक स्थापना हुई?
o: Second Judges Case (1993) — later expanded in Third Judges Case (1998)
e:
The Second Judges Case (Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India, 1993) established the Collegium System (CJI + 2 senior-most judges), which was expanded in the Third Judges Case (1998) to CJI + 4 senior-most judges.
द्वितीय न्यायाधीश मामले (1993) में कॉलेजियम प्रणाली स्थापित हुई तथा तृतीय मामले (1998) में इसका विस्तार (CJI + 4 वरिष्ठ न्यायाधीश) हुआ।
Booster Facts: (1) In 2015 (Fourth Judges Case), the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Constitutional Amendment & NJAC Act as violating Judicial Independence (Basic Structure).
qe: In which landmark Supreme Court judgment was the 'Collegium System' for the appointment of Supreme Court and High Court judges formally established (giving primacy to the CJI's opinion formed in consultation with senior judges)?
oe: Second Judges Case (1993) — later expanded in Third Judges Case (1998)

q: 1970–80 के दशक में भारत में 'जनहित याचिका' (PIL) के जनक/प्रणेता के रूप में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के किन पूर्व न्यायाधीशों को जाना जाता है?
o: Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer
Justice H.J. Kania and Justice M. Patanjali Sastri
Justice A.N. Ray and Justice Y.V. Chandrachud
Justice Ranjan Gogoi and Justice S.A. Bobde
e:
Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer pioneered PIL in India by relaxing the traditional rule of 'Locus Standi' (standing to sue), allowing public-spirited citizens to approach courts for marginalized groups (e.g., Hussainara Khatoon, 1979).
न्यायमूर्ति पी.एन. भगवती तथा न्यायमूर्ति वी.आर. कृष्ण अय्यर भारत में जनहित याचिका (PIL) के प्रणेता माने जाते हैं।
Booster Facts: (1) PIL originated in the USA in the 1960s. (2) Pushpa Kapila Hingorani is known as the 'Mother of PIL' in India.
qe: Who among the following former Supreme Court Justices are hailed as the pioneers of Public Interest Litigation (PIL / जनहित याचिका) in India during the late 1970s–80s?
oe: Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer
Justice H.J. Kania and Justice M. Patanjali Sastri
Justice A.N. Ray and Justice Y.V. Chandrachud
Justice Ranjan Gogoi and Justice S.A. Bobde

q: अनुच्छेद 226 के अंतर्गत उच्च न्यायालय की रिट अधिकारिता को अनुच्छेद 32 के अंतर्गत सर्वोच्च न्यायालय की रिट अधिकारिता से अधिक व्यापक क्यों माना जाता है?
o: High Courts can issue writs only for Fundamental Rights, whereas Supreme Court issues them for all legal rights.
High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights AND any other legal/statutory right ('for any other purpose'), whereas Supreme Court under Art. 32 issues them only for Fundamental Rights.
High Courts have territorial jurisdiction over the entire country, whereas Supreme Court does not.
High Courts are bound to issue writs under Art. 226 as a Fundamental Right, whereas Art. 32 is discretionary.
e:
Under Article 226, High Courts can issue writs for enforcing Fundamental Rights AND 'for any other purpose' (ordinary legal rights), whereas the Supreme Court under Article 32 can issue writs ONLY for Fundamental Rights (though Art. 32 itself is a Fundamental Right, while Art. 226 is discretionary).
अनुच्छेद 226 के तहत उच्च न्यायालय मौलिक अधिकारों के साथ-साथ अन्य विधिक अधिकारों के लिए भी रिट जारी कर सकता है।
Booster Facts: (1) Five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, Quo Warranto. (2) Transfer of High Court judges is governed by Article 222.
qe: Why is the Writ Jurisdiction of a High Court under Article 226 considered WIDER than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32?
oe: High Courts can issue writs only for Fundamental Rights, whereas Supreme Court issues them for all legal rights.
High Courts can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights AND any other legal/statutory right ('for any other purpose'), whereas Supreme Court under Art. 32 issues them only for Fundamental Rights.
High Courts have territorial jurisdiction over the entire country, whereas Supreme Court does not.

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 143 के अंतर्गत राष्ट्रपति सर्वोच्च न्यायालय से परामर्श (Advisory Opinion) माँग सकते हैं। अनुच्छेद 143 के बारे में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही है?
o: The Supreme Court's advisory opinion is strictly binding on the President in all matters.
On pre-constitutional treaty disputes (Art. 143(2)), the Supreme Court MUST tender its opinion, though the opinion is NOT binding on the President.
The Supreme Court has no right to decline tendering advice on a question of public importance under Art. 143(1).
Only the Prime Minister can directly refer a matter to the Supreme Court under Article 143.
e:
Under Art. 143(1) (question of law/fact of public importance), SC MAY tender or decline advice; under Art. 143(2) (pre-constitutional treaty/agreement), SC MUST tender advice. In BOTH cases, the opinion is advisory and NOT binding on the President.
अनुच्छेद 143(2) में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को परामर्श देना अनिवार्य है, किंतु राष्ट्रपति परामर्श मानने हेतु बाध्य नहीं हैं।
Booster Facts: (1) Removal of SC/HC Judges (Art. 124(4)) requires an address by both Houses passed by special majority on grounds of 'proved misbehaviour or incapacity' (Judges Enquiry Act, 1968).
qe: Under Article 143 of the Indian Constitution, the President may seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court. Which of the following statements about Article 143 is correct?
oe: The Supreme Court's advisory opinion is strictly binding on the President in all matters.
On pre-constitutional treaty disputes (Art. 143(2)), the Supreme Court MUST tender its opinion, though the opinion is NOT binding on the President.
The Supreme Court has no right to decline tendering advice on a question of public importance under Art. 143(1).
Only the Prime Minister can directly refer a matter to the Supreme Court under Article 143.

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 155 तथा 156 के अंतर्गत किसी राज्य के राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति किसके द्वारा की जाती है और वह किसके प्रसादपर्यंत पद धारण करता है?
e:
The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal (Art. 155) and holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art. 156; normal term 5 years).
राज्यपाल की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति करते हैं और वे राष्ट्रपति के प्रसादपर्यंत पद धारण करते हैं।
Booster Facts: (1) 7th Constitutional Amendment Act (1956) allowed the same person to be appointed Governor for two or more States. (2) Minimum age for Governor = 35 years (Art. 157).
qe: Under Article 155 and Article 156 of the Indian Constitution, the Governor of a State is appointed by and holds office during the pleasure of:

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 200 के अंतर्गत निम्नलिखित में से किस स्थिति में राज्यपाल के लिए राज्य विधानमंडल द्वारा पारित विधेयक को राष्ट्रपति के विचारार्थ आरक्षित करना अनिवार्य है?
o: Any Ordinary Bill involving state taxation
Any Bill concerning rural local bodies
Any Money Bill passed by the Vidhan Sabha
Any Bill that in the Governor's opinion would so derogate from the powers of the High Court as to endanger its constitutional position
e:
Article 200 makes it mandatory for the Governor to reserve a Bill if it endangers the constitutional position of the State High Court. Other discretionary reservations include Bills violating Directive Principles, national interest, or Art. 31A.
यदि कोई विधेयक उच्च न्यायालय की संवैधानिक स्थिति को खतरे में डालता हो, तो अनुच्छेद 200 के तहत उसे राष्ट्रपति हेतु आरक्षित करना अनिवार्य है।
Booster Facts: (1) Article 163 explicitly recognizes the Governor's 'constitutional discretion' (unlike the President under Art. 74). (2) Article 201 deals with the President's action on reserved state bills.
qe: Under Article 200 of the Indian Constitution, in which of the following cases is it MANDATORY for the Governor to reserve a Bill passed by the State Legislature for the consideration of the President?
oe: Any Ordinary Bill involving state taxation
Any Bill concerning rural local bodies
Any Money Bill passed by the Vidhan Sabha
Any Bill that in the Governor's opinion would so derogate from the powers of the High Court as to endanger its constitutional position

q: कौन-सा अनुच्छेद किसी राज्य के राज्यपाल को राज्य विधानमंडल के विश्रांतिकाल में अध्यादेश (Ordinance) प्रख्यापित करने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है?
e:
Article 213 empowers the Governor to promulgate Ordinances when the State Legislature is not in session (mirroring the President's power under Article 123 — note the digit transposition 123 ↔ 213!).
अनुच्छेद 213 राज्यपाल को अध्यादेश जारी करने की शक्ति देता है।
Booster Facts: (1) Article 161 = Governor's pardoning power (cannot pardon death sentences or court-martial sentences). (2) Governor requires prior instructions from the President to promulgate an ordinance on matters requiring Presidential sanction/reservation.
qe: Which Article empowers the Governor of a State to promulgate Ordinances during the recess of the State Legislature?

q: वर्तमान में भारत के कितने राज्यों में द्विसदनीय राज्य विधानमंडल (विधानसभा एवं विधान परिषद दोनों) है?
e:
Exactly 6 Indian States have a Bicameral Legislature: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana. (J&K's Legislative Council was abolished in 2019.)
वर्तमान में 6 राज्यों (यूपी, बिहार, महाराष्ट्र, कर्नाटक, आंध्र प्रदेश, तेलंगाना) में द्विसदनीय विधानमंडल है।
Booster Facts: (1) Uttar Pradesh has the largest Vidhan Sabha (403 elected seats) and largest Vidhan Parishad (100 seats) in India.
qe: Currently, how many Indian States have a Bicameral State Legislature (both Vidhan Sabha and Vidhan Parishad)?

q: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 169 के अंतर्गत किसी राज्य में विधान परिषद का सृजन (स्थापना) या उत्सादन (समाप्ति) कैसे किया जा सकता है?
o: By the Governor through an executive order
By Parliament through a simple majority, provided the concerned State Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority
Only by a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368 requiring ratification by half the states
By the Rajya Sabha alone with a 2/3rd majority
e:
Under Article 169, Parliament may create or abolish a Vidhan Parishad by simple majority (NOT deemed an amendment under Art. 368) if the State Vidhan Sabha passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority (majority of total membership + 2/3rd of members present and voting).
संबंधित राज्य की विधानसभा द्वारा विशेष बहुमत से प्रस्ताव पारित होने पर संसद साधारण बहुमत से विधान परिषद का सृजन या समाप्ति कर सकती है।
Booster Facts: (1) Under Art. 171, Vidhan Parishad strength is max 1/3rd of Vidhan Sabha and min 40. Composition: 1/3 MLAs, 1/3 Local Bodies, 1/12 Graduates, 1/12 Teachers, 1/6 Governor-nominated.
qe: Under Article 169 of the Indian Constitution, how can a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) be created or abolished?
oe: By the Governor through an executive order
By Parliament through a simple majority, provided the concerned State Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority

q: भारत में किसी राज्य का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी कौन होता है, जिसकी नियुक्ति राज्यपाल द्वारा अनुच्छेद 165 के अंतर्गत की जाती है?
e:
Under Article 165, the Advocate General (महाधिवक्ता) is the highest law officer of the State, qualified to be appointed a High Court Judge. He has the right to speak and take part in State Legislature proceedings without voting (Art. 177).
अनुच्छेद 165 के अंतर्गत राज्य का सर्वोच्च विधि अधिकारी 'महाधिवक्ता (Advocate General)' होता है।
Booster Facts: (1) Attorney General of India (Art. 76) is the highest law officer of the Union. (2) Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor under Article 164.
qe: Who is the highest law officer of a State in India, appointed by the Governor under Article 165?

q: भारत में 'जिला कलेक्टर' (District Collector) का पद सर्वप्रथम 1772 में बंगाल के किस ब्रिटिश गवर्नर-जनरल द्वारा सृजित किया गया था?
e:
Warren Hastings created the post of District Collector in 1772 to supervise land revenue collection and judicial administration at the district level. Lord Cornwallis (1793) later separated judicial powers from the Collector.
1772 में वारेन हेस्टिंग्स ने भारत में जिला कलेक्टर का पद सृजित किया था।
Booster Facts: (1) Lord Cornwallis is called the 'Father of Civil Services in India'. (2) Lord Ripon's 1882 Resolution is the 'Magna Carta of Local Self-Government in India'.
qe: The office of the 'District Collector' (जिला कलेक्टर) in India was first created in 1772 by which British Governor-General of Bengal?

q: भारतीय जिला प्रशासन में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा जिला मजिस्ट्रेट / कलेक्टर (DM) का कार्य नहीं है?
o: Maintenance of land records and collection of land revenue
Maintenance of law and order as head of the district criminal administration
Acting as District Election Officer and Chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)
Delivering binding judicial verdicts in murder trials as Sessions Judge
e:
Under Article 50 (Separation of Judiciary from Executive), criminal trials for heinous offences like murder are presided over by the District & Sessions Judge (independent judiciary), NOT by the District Magistrate (Executive Magistrate).
अनुच्छेद 50 (कार्यपालिका का न्यायपालिका से पृथक्करण) के कारण हत्या जैसे मुकदमों की सुनवाई सत्र न्यायाधीश करते हैं, DM नहीं।
Booster Facts: (1) DM chairs the DDMA under the Disaster Management Act, 2005. (2) In Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, the officer is called District Magistrate (DM); in Rajasthan/MP/Maharashtra, District Collector; in Punjab/Haryana, Deputy Commissioner (DC).
qe: Which of the following is NOT a function of the District Magistrate / Collector in Indian district administration?
oe: Maintenance of land records and collection of land revenue
Maintenance of law and order as head of the district criminal administration
Acting as District Election Officer and Chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA)
Delivering binding judicial verdicts in murder trials as Sessions Judge

q: लोकतांत्रिक विकेंद्रीकरण के संदर्भ में द्वितीय प्रशासनिक सुधार आयोग (2nd ARC, 2007) ने पंचायती राज संस्थाओं के संदर्भ में जिला कलेक्टर की भूमिका पर क्या सिफारिश की थी?

Booster Facts: (1) First ARC (1966) was chaired by Morarji Desai (later K. Hanumanthaiya). (2) In UP, CDO (Chief Development Officer) assists in rural development coordination alongside DM.
qe: In the context of democratic decentralization, what did the Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2nd ARC, 2007) recommend regarding the role of the District Collector vis-à-vis Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)?
oe: Abolish Zila Parishads and hand all local funds exclusively to the Collector
Keep the District Collector focused on regulatory/revenue functions while empowering Zila Parishad with a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) for development works, ensuring coordination
Make the District Collector an elected political representative
Merge the District Collector's office with the High Court

q: जहाँ बलवंत राय मेहता समिति (1957) ने त्रि-स्तरीय पंचायती राज व्यवस्था की सिफारिश की थी, वहीं 1977 में किस समिति ने इसके स्थान पर द्वि-स्तरीय व्यवस्था (जिला परिषद और मंडल पंचायत) की सिफारिश की थी?
e:
The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977, appointed by the Janata Government) recommended a 2-tier system (Zila Parishad at district level and Mandal Panchayat for a group of villages) and open participation of political parties in Panchayat elections.
अशोक मेहता समिति (1977) ने द्वि-स्तरीय पंचायती राज व्यवस्था की सिफारिश की थी।
Booster Facts: (1) Balwant Rai Mehta is called the 'Architect of Panchayati Raj in India'. (2) Rajasthan (Nagaur, 2 Oct 1959) was the first state, and Andhra Pradesh (11 Oct 1959) the second state to adopt Panchayati Raj.
qe: While the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) recommended a 3-tier Panchayati Raj structure, which committee in 1977 recommended replacing it with a 2-tier system (Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat)?

q: 73वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992 के अंतर्गत निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सभी राज्यों के लिए एक 'अनिवार्य' (compulsory) प्रावधान है, न कि स्वैच्छिक प्रावधान?
o: Reservation of seats for Backward Classes (OBCs) in Panchayats
Granting voting rights to MPs and MLAs in Panchayats
Reservation of not less than one-third (33%) of seats for women and a minimum age of 21 years to contest Panchayat elections
Assigning all 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects automatically with full taxation powers
e:
Compulsory provisions of the 73rd Amendment include: Gram Sabha (Art. 243A), 3-tier system (states >20 lakh pop.), direct elections to all seats, 21 years minimum age, 5-year tenure (fresh polls within 6 months if dissolved), SC/ST & 1/3rd Women reservation (Art. 243D), State Election Commission (243K), and State Finance Commission (243I). OBC reservation and MP/MLA representation are voluntary.
महिलाओं के लिए कम से कम 1/3 आरक्षण और चुनाव लड़ने की न्यूनतम आयु 21 वर्ष अनिवार्य प्रावधान हैं।
qe: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which of the following is a COMPULSORY (mandatory) provision for all states, and NOT a voluntary provision?
oe: Reservation of seats for Backward Classes (OBCs) in Panchayats
Granting voting rights to MPs and MLAs in Panchayats
Reservation of not less than one-third (33%) of seats for women and a minimum age of 21 years to contest Panchayat elections
Assigning all 29 Eleventh Schedule subjects automatically with full taxation powers

q: भारतीय संविधान के कौन-से दो अनुच्छेद पंचायतों के लिए क्रमशः 'राज्य वित्त आयोग' तथा 'राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग' का प्रावधान करते हैं?
e:
Article 243-I mandates the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission every 5 years to review Panchayat finances (also covers Municipalities via Art. 243-Y). Article 243-K establishes the State Election Commission to conduct Panchayat/Municipal elections.
अनुच्छेद 243-I राज्य वित्त आयोग तथा अनुच्छेद 243-K राज्य निर्वाचन आयोग से संबंधित है।
Booster Facts: (1) Art. 243-A = Gram Sabha; Art. 243-D = Reservation of seats; Art. 243-G = Powers & responsibilities of Panchayats.
qe: Which two Articles of the Indian Constitution provide for the 'State Finance Commission' and the 'State Election Commission' for Panchayats respectively?

q: 74वें संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1992 (भाग IXA, अनुच्छेद 243-Q) द्वारा संवैधानिक रूप से किन तीन प्रकार की नगरपालिकाओं का प्रावधान किया गया है?
o: Gram Panchayat, Block Samiti, Zila Parishad
Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council (Nagar Palika Parishad), Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam)
District Board, Town Area Committee, Metropolitan Council
e:
Article 243-Q mandates three Urban Local Bodies: (1) Nagar Panchayat (transitional rural-to-urban area), (2) Municipal Council (smaller urban area), and (3) Municipal Corporation (larger urban area). The 12th Schedule lists 18 urban subjects.
अनुच्छेद 243-Q तीन प्रकार की शहरी निकायों— नगर पंचायत, नगर पालिका परिषद तथा नगर निगम का प्रावधान करता है।
Booster Facts: (1) Madras Municipal Corporation (1687–88) was India's first Municipal Corporation. (2) Art. 243-ZD = District Planning Committee (DPC); Art. 243-ZE = Metropolitan Planning Committee (MPC).
qe: Which three types of Municipalities are constitutionally mandated by the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Part IXA, Article 243-Q)?
oe: Gram Panchayat, Block Samiti, Zila Parishad
Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council (Nagar Palika Parishad), Municipal Corporation (Nagar Nigam)
District Board, Town Area Committee, Metropolitan Council

q: पाँचवीं अनुसूची के जनजातीय क्षेत्रों में स्वशासन की सुरक्षा के साथ भाग IX का विस्तार करने वाला 'पेसा अधिनियम, 1996' (PESA Act) किस समिति की सिफारिश पर अधिनियमित किया गया था?
e:
PESA Act, 1996 was enacted on the recommendation of the Dileep Singh Bhuria Committee (1995). It empowers the Gram Sabha in Fifth Schedule areas (10 states) over minor forest produce (MFP), land alienation, and local markets.

e:
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel (celebrated as the 'Patron Saint of India's Civil Services' — National Civil Services Day is observed on 21 April in honour of his 1947 address to IAS probationers) defended All India Services as the 'Steel Frame' of unified India.

Max Weber proposed the Legal-Rational Authority and Ideal-Type Bureaucracy model. In parliamentary democracies like India, civil servants also uphold 'Political Neutrality' (implementing elected governments' policies impartially) and 'Anonymity'.

q: अनुच्छेद 317 के अंतर्गत 'कदाचार' (misbehaviour) के आधार पर राज्य लोक सेवा आयोग (SPSC) के अध्यक्ष या सदस्य को पद से हटाने का संवैधानिक अधिकार किसे है?

The Chief Justice of the State High Court
e:

Booster Facts: (1) Tenure of UPSC members: 6 years or 65 years of age; SPSC members: 6 years or 62 years of age (41st Amendment, 1976 raised SPSC age from 60 to 62).
qe: Who has the constitutional authority to remove the Chairman or a Member of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC) on the ground of 'misbehaviour' (Article 317)?
oe: The President of India (only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court)
The Chief Justice of the State High Court

q: भारतीय संविधान का कौन-सा अनुच्छेद सिविल सेवकों को संवैधानिक संरक्षण प्रदान करता है कि किसी भी सिविल सेवक को उसकी नियुक्ति करने वाले प्राधिकारी से अधीनस्थ प्राधिकारी द्वारा या सुनवाई का उचित अवसर दिए बिना बर्खास्त नहीं किया जा सकता?

q: 'ओम्बुड्समैन' (Ombudsman) संस्था का उद्भव 1809 में किस देश में हुआ था तथा 1963 में भारतीय शब्द 'लोकपाल' और 'लोकायुक्त' किसने गढ़े थे?

Sweden established the world's first Ombudsman in 1809. In India, jurist Dr. L.M. Singhvi coined the terms 'Lokpal' and 'Lokayukta' in 1963, and the First ARC (1966, Morarji Desai) formally recommended establishing them.

q: लोकपाल और लोकायुक्त अधिनियम, 2013 के अंतर्गत लोकपाल संस्था की अधिकतम सांविधिक संरचना क्या है?

oe: 1 Chairperson and up to 8 Members (50% Judicial; 50% from SC/ST/OBC/Minorities/Women)

q: 1971 में लोकायुक्त संस्था की स्थापना करने वाला भारत का प्रथम राज्य कौन-सा था तथा उत्तर प्रदेश लोकायुक्त अधिनियम, 1975 के अंतर्गत उत्तर प्रदेश के प्रथम लोकायुक्त किसे नियुक्त किया गया था?
